correct_answer: 10s — the Confluence page (version 4) is the runbook-linked authoritative source and it still specifies 10s flat default
rationale: The authoritative source is what is actually deployed and documented. SRE-2201 was completed (status: Done) on March 22, setting the timeout to 10s. This was reflected in Confluence version 4 (edited Mar 24). SRE-2287, which calls for 5s, is still in 'Open' status — it was never implemented. Jordan's Slack message agreeing to the tiered approach was informal direction that was never acted upon (no Confluence edit was made, no deploy occurred). The on-call runbook points to Confluence v4 which states 10s. Answer A confuses a Slack conversation about intent with an actual configuration change — the Confluence page was never updated. Answer C invents a 'latest postmortem wins' rule that doesn't exist; postmortem action items only take effect when completed. Answer D incorrectly assumes that because SRE-2287 is open, the change from SRE-2201 was also reverted — but SRE-2201 is Done and its 10s change is in production.
